review_state: PARTIAL; six extracted appointment calendar/create/action paths reviewed; browser/accessibility, no-show domain semantics, runtime authorization/idempotency, remaining paths, fixture provenance, and independent critique remain open

paths_reviewed.review_notes: Presentational child reads typed props and emits appointment, date, view, slot and workflow intent; no service/API call or local domain state was found. Responsive/dark-theme CSS and native focus styles exist, but browser/viewport proof is absent.

The component owns only local selector/quick-create modal state, resets it when the controlled open prop changes, maps an optional slot preset, and emits close/created. Service persistence remains in the parent quick-create form and caller.

Actions fail closed on the client for permission/status, serialize concurrent UI actions, clear stale local work by generation on invalidation, and refresh overview after successful mutations. The controller has no client request cancellation or idempotency key; server authorization/retry semantics were not established by its fake-service tests.

Three component tests cover list rendering, a slot event and a dense-slot view-change event using props and stubs. They do not assert actual keyboard navigation, focus order, screen-reader semantics, responsive layout or visual output.
Three tests stub modal, client selector and quick-create form; they cover slot preset propagation, event forwarding, and local state reset without service/network calls.

Five controller tests cover client permission/status eligibility, check-in contract, queue no-show versus appointment-cancel fallback, serialized actions/invalidation, and appointment cancellation using fake services.

source_diff_and_contracts.parent_wiring: AppointmentsListPage.vue supplies child props and handles emitted intents; source review round 10 covers parent ownership and overview loading.
source_diff_and_contracts.action_service_contract: checkInQueue sends appointment/patient/owner/reason/priority; queue no-show is selected only when operational.queueEntryId exists; otherwise markNoShow calls cancelAppointment with reason 'No-show registrado pela agenda'.
source_diff_and_contracts.targeted_backend_semantics: Targeted static inspection found /queue/:id/no-show requires scheduling.manage and records an audit action no_show, while /appointments/:id/cancel transitions appointment status to cancelled and records cancel_appointment. No dedicated appointment no-show endpoint was found in the inspected routes.
source_diff_and_contracts.accessibility_contract: AgendaCalendarOrList applies role=grid and labels the week/day containers, but the inspected component contains no role=row/role=gridcell and no keydown/arrow navigation handler. It has native buttons and visible focus styles, but the full interactive grid pattern is not demonstrated.
source_diff_and_contracts.assessment: The components preserve explicit parent ownership, but grid semantics and the no-show-versus-cancel domain behavior need confirmed product/QA decisions before candidate acceptance; neither is treated as an established runtime defect in this source-only round.

test_execution.environment: Standalone SPA Vitest/JSDOM config. Component tests use Vue Test Utils stubs; action-controller services are in-memory fakes. No database global setup, provider, or live network call was observed.

findings_and_limits.observation: For an appointment without a queueEntryId, the UI action labeled no-show calls appointment cancellation. The inspected backend returns status cancelled and an audit action cancel_appointment; queue-backed no-show uses a separate endpoint and audit action no_show.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Product/QA must confirm that a cancelled appointment with this reason is the intended no-show record/reporting contract, or identify the required appointment no-show transition. This review does not infer intent.

findings_and_limits.observation: The component marks week/day containers role=grid but does not expose rows/gridcells or implement grid arrow-key navigation in the inspected source. The component tests do not cover screen-reader or keyboard interaction.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Validate with keyboard and assistive technology and choose a complete grid interaction model or a semantic layout that does not promise unsupported grid behavior.

findings_and_limits.observation: Client permission checks and action generation protect UI state, but mocked tests do not establish server authorization, tenant isolation, mutation idempotency, or behavior after a request is already sent.
findings_and_limits.required_followup: Verify the API boundary under an approved disposable/no-connection test setup before claiming mutation authorization or retry safety.

candidate_actions.hold_reason: The six paths are hash-stable and focused tests pass, but Product/QA must resolve no-show semantics, calendar grid accessibility remains unverified, backend authorization/retry semantics and fixture provenance remain open, other appointment paths and the full inventory are pending, and no independent critique has occurred.

limitations: The 11 tests run in JSDOM with component stubs and fake services; they do not prove browser keyboard/focus, screen-reader behavior, viewport/visual QA, API persistence, authorization, tenant isolation, or idempotency.
The current code maps no-show without a queue entry to cancellation; business acceptance of that mapping is unresolved, not presumed wrong or right.
The reviewed test fixtures include person/patient-shaped names that appear synthetic; their provenance was not confirmed, and no full privacy review was performed.

This round covers only the two extracted Vue components, the action controller and their three tests. It does not cover the other original-inventory paths or independently approve candidate inclusion.
